newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for 30,000T raw sugar on Jan 30.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 30,000T raw sugar on Jan 30.

text.p: State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp will tender on January 30 in New York for a 30,000-tonne shipment of raw sugar to fulfil its current fiscal buying plan, a company official said on Friday.
The tender, which falls on January 31 Taiwan time, will be by invitation only in New York City and will specify April 20 to May 5 delivery to Taiwan, the official said.
The state company is on track to import 120,000 tonnes of sugar in fiscal year 1996/97, which began on July 1, officials have said.

Taiwan Sugar has bought 90,000 tonnes of sugar in the fiscal year to date, including 60,000 tonnes arranged through a three-year supply deal negotiated privately with British specialist supplier Czarnikow Sugar.
The 60,000 tonnes per year Czarnikow pact took effect in 1997, but leaves Taiwan Sugar 30,000 tonnes short of fulfilling its 120,000 tonne fiscal purchasing plan.
Taiwan Sugar, like most state companies on the rapidly liberalising island, is under mandate to privatise.
But the cabinet ruled on June 27 that it would not face serious competition before 2002.
